name: Scaleway Apple silicon (Mac mini)

modes.label: Hourly, no commitment (24 h minimum for macOS)
modes.note: Whole physical Mac mini per server. EUR list price x 1.17 USD/EUR, before tax. "The minimum lease period for Apple silicon is 24 hours due to licensing restrictions"; billed while assigned to the account (even idle/powered off) until deleted. Scaleway publishes no monthly cap on hourly billing; month_cap = 730 x hourly is the bound for one Mac kept leased all month and reused across sessions (avoids paying the 24 h minimum per session). It is NOT the monthly-commitment price (that is the always-on-commit mode). Up to 2 macOS VMs per Mac under the Apple SLA.

modes.label: Monthly commitment (auto-renewing)
modes.commit_note: Initial commitment 1 month from order, auto-renews monthly on the anniversary date; deleting the machine takes effect on the anniversary date; cannot switch back from commitment to hourly.
modes.note: hour = monthly price / 730 (for comparison); month_cap = monthly price (EUR x 1.17).

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Private Network for Apple silicon option: EUR 9.99/month or EUR 0.03/hour (1 Gbps), EUR 19.99/month or EUR 0.06/hour (10 Gbps), not modelled. Options stay without commitment even on a committed Mac.

caveats: Currency: list prices in EUR excl. VAT, converted at 1.17 USD/EUR (repo assumption).
Billing granularity after the 24 h minimum assumed hourly (prices shown per hour); not stated explicitly.
Per-instance engine sizing picks one Mac per session; with the Apple 2-VM cap two 4 vCPU / 8 GiB VMs can share a 16 GB Mac (DIY with UTM/Tart), halving machine count.
Only PAR-1 availability zone shown on the pricing page. Egress pricing and IPv4 pricing not stated on the Apple silicon pricing page (null).
Asahi Linux variant (M2-L-ASAHI, EUR 139/mo / EUR 0.21/h) has no 24 h minimum; not modelled as a macOS mode.
Research file named the M4 Pro SKU "M4-L"; live page calls it M4-XL (14-core, 64 GB, 2.05 TB).

Public bandwidth upgrade options (M4-M and M4-XL only, 'Up to 10 Gbps'; 1 Gbps included): 2 Gbps EUR 99.99/mo or EUR 0.274/h; 3 Gbps 149.99 / 0.411; 4 Gbps 199.99 / 0.548; 5 Gbps 249.99 / 0.685; 6 Gbps 289.99 / 0.795; 7 Gbps 329.99 / 0.904; 8 Gbps 369.99 / 1.014; 9 Gbps 409.99 / 1.123; 10 Gbps 449.99 / 1.233, unlimited traffic; first month prorated.
Zones: M1-M is sold in fr-par-1 and fr-par-3 (docs: 'Mac mini M1 are available in PARIS 3'); M2/M2 Pro/M4 in fr-par-1 only. Still region eu (Paris).

Asahi Linux (M2-L-ASAHI, 412 GB) is 'currently in experimental status'; M4 FAQ says 'Linux OS or Windows OS are not supported' on M4. features.linux=true relies only on this experimental M2 Pro variant.

M4-L was a separate M4 Pro SKU (EUR 305/month, EUR 0.44/h, fr-par-1 and fr-par-3) that the public catalog now marks "status": "retired"; the live M4 Pro SKU is M4-XL (14-core, 64 GB, 2.05 TB, EUR 335/month, EUR 0.49/h).
Billing continues until deletion completes (~30 min after the request) and powering off a Mac mini does not stop billing; hourly SKUs in the public catalog use unit hour (granularity_s 3600 kept).

fleet.verification: Validated payment method; newer Mac shapes require identity validation.
fleet.tiers: Per AZ/shape: payment-only M1-M and M2-M allow 1 each; identity-verified quotas M1-M 3, M2-M/M2-L 5, M4-S/M4-M 2, M4-XL 1. Support beyond those.
fleet.notes: No single account-wide count: quotas are per shape and Availability Zone. M4 shapes are gated by identity validation; do not treat a one-Mac allowance as universal across types.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Backups and snapshots must be configured by you. Refer to our documentation for assistance in setting up backups for Dedibox, Elastic Metal, and Apple silicon.
snapshot_auto.note: Dedicated Mac mini; internal SSD just persists while the Mac is assigned. No stop/sleep state (billed until deleted).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can back up your Mac mini using a backup solution of your choice. Examples include: Restic for command-line backups. Arq Backup for graphical interface backups. Both solutions allow you to store backups on our Object Storage.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Apple silicon API has only create/update/delete/reboot/reinstall/private-network/runner endpoints (Go SDK applesilicon v1alpha1); no snapshot or image endpoint. Reinstall wipes the disk. Time Machine system restore is blocked by MDM profiles.

harness_api.note: API manages the bare-metal Mac lifecycle only (servers, OS, commitment, bandwidth, Private Networks, GitHub/GitLab CI runners via Dev OS). No agent-harness or exec API.

egress_allowlist.quote: Network ACLs only control traffic as it enters or exits the Private Network(s) of a VPC. They do not: ... Filter traffic from/to the public internet (for this, use security groups for Instances, or equivalent features for other resource types)
egress_allowlist.note: Security groups are an Instances (and Elastic Metal) feature; nothing equivalent is documented for Apple silicon, whose public connectivity 'cannot be disabled at any stage'. VPC Network ACLs (ip-level, stateless) can filter traffic between Private Networks only. The remove-public-IP guide routes egress via a Public Gateway, but the IP is removed inside macOS (networksetup), so a root agent can undo it.

egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side egress filtering of any kind for Mac minis, so no HTTP-level rules.

ingress_rules.quote: For some products, e.g. Apple silicon, public connectivity cannot be disabled at any stage
ingress_rules.note: Mac mini always has a public IPv4 + IPv6 /128 with no security group / cloud firewall. Only guest-side controls: preinstalled fail2ban for VNC, pf rules (documented), or disabling the public interface inside macOS and reaching it via Private Network + Public Gateway SSH bastion (Private Network option EUR 9.99/mo 1 Gbps, EUR 19.99/mo 10 Gbps). VPC Network ACLs apply only between Private Networks.

guest_firewall.quote: Enabling and configuring Packet Filter (pf) 1. Open the pf configuration file in a text editor to restrict access to screen sharing: sudo nano /etc/pf.conf
guest_firewall.note: Bare-metal Mac mini with sudo; macOS pf (not nftables/iptables). Scaleway's own docs show pf rules; SIP cannot be disabled and MDM profiles restrict some admin actions, but pf works.

secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy for Mac minis; Scaleway Secret Manager is a separate store you fetch from yourself, not an injecting proxy in front of the sandbox.

volume_attach.quote: Block Storage volumes are compatible with Scaleway Instances, Managed Dabatase for PostgreSQL and MySQL, and Kubernetes Kapsule clusters.
volume_attach.note: Storage is the Mac mini's internal SSD only (256 GB to 2.05 TB by shape). Kernel-extension option allows DIY macFUSE mounts of remote storage.

volume_shared.quote: Scaleway File Storage is designed to be used in conjunction with Scaleway Instances and Kubernetes Kapsule.
volume_shared.note: No first-party shared filesystem for Mac minis; DIY via Object Storage / SMB / macFUSE.

isolation.quote: You don't have access to the physical machine, thus no access to macOS recovery.
isolation.note: Each server is a whole physical Mac mini assigned to one customer account (not a shared/virtualized macOS instance); the API's own docs describe creating/deleting a physical server.

image_oci.quote: Select an operating system version. If you choose a macOS version different from the default one, expect a delay of approximately 1 hour before the Mac mini becomes available.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only Scaleway/Apple-provided OS choices (macOS versions, Dev OS, Asahi Linux) can be selected at creation; there is no custom Docker/OCI image or BYOI mechanism (API has no image endpoint, only reinstall with a chosen OS version).

docker_inside.quote: UTM is a free and open-source software that leverages Apple's Hypervisor framework and QEMU to provide virtualization capabilities.
docker_inside.note: derived: root/sudo access plus working nested virtualization (Apple's Hypervisor framework, used for UTM VMs) on bare-metal Apple silicon lets a user install Docker Desktop or Colima (both use the same Virtualization framework) via Homebrew; not separately documented by Scaleway.

anti_bot.quote: Apple silicon as-a-Service is tailored for developing, building, testing, and signing applications for Apple devices such as iPhones, iPads, Mac computers, and more.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a bare-metal Mac mini for building/CI, not a browser-automation or scraping product.

captcha_solving.quote: Apple silicon as-a-Service is tailored for developing, building, testing, and signing applications for Apple devices such as iPhones, iPads, Mac computers, and more.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Each Mac mini can have one IPv4 address and one IPv6 subnet (/128).
egress_ip_type.note: Datacenter IP in a Scaleway facility (Paris), fixed to the machine for as long as it is leased (card already marks static_egress_ip=true).

live_resize.quote: Whole physical Mac mini per server.
live_resize.note: Each server is one physical Mac mini of a fixed shape (M1-M, M2-M, M4-S, etc.); changing CPU/RAM requires deleting and recreating the server with a different type, not a live resize of a running machine.

own_agent_api.note: The Apple silicon API only manages server lifecycle (create/delete/reboot/reinstall/private-network); there is no first-party agent (browser/computer-use/research) API of any kind.

mcp_server.note: No MCP server is documented for Apple silicon / Bare Metal server management; Scaleway's public docs and API reference for this product only expose a REST API and CLI/Terraform wrappers.

lang_python.quote: Open-source licenses (MIT, GPL, Apache, etc.) for tools such as Homebrew, Node.js, and Python
lang_python.note: A default Standard macOS install ships bare (Xcode, MacPorts, fail2ban, scw-agent only, per the FAQ) and does not include Python/Node out of the box; but Scaleway's own selectable Dev OS image (mirroring the GitHub Actions macOS-15 runner) comes pre-installed with Python and multiple language runtimes.

lang_node.quote: Open-source licenses (MIT, GPL, Apache, etc.) for tools such as Homebrew, Node.js, and Python
lang_node.note: Same as lang_python: not in the bare Standard macOS install, but included in Scaleway's selectable Dev OS image (GitHub Actions macOS-15 runner parity, which ships Node.js).

soc2.quote: Compliance GDPR HDS ISO/IEC 27001 ISO/IEC 27001 SoA CSA STAR Level 1
soc2.note: Scaleway's own Trust Center lists its compliance certifications explicitly (GDPR, HDS, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27001 SoA, CSA STAR Level 1); SOC 2 is not among them.

hipaa.quote: Compliance GDPR HDS ISO/IEC 27001 ISO/IEC 27001 SoA CSA STAR Level 1
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. HIPAA/BAA is not listed among Scaleway's compliance certifications; Scaleway is a French/EU-based provider whose health-data certification is the French HDS scheme, not the US HIPAA framework.

sso.quote: Scaleway supports Identity Federation to provide your teams with secure access to their accounts via Single Sign-On (SSO). Depending on your organization's requirements, you can use either built-in OAuth2 providers or configure SAML for centralized identity management.
sso.note: Account/organization-level SSO (OAuth2 by default, SAML with setup) applies across all Scaleway products including Apple silicon.

max_session_h.quote: Yes, you pay for your Mac mini as long as it is assigned to your account. You must explicitly delete it in the console or via the CLI to stop charges.
max_session_h.note: A Mac mini runs indefinitely until the customer deletes it; the only limit is a 24-hour *minimum* lease before deletion is allowed, not a maximum session length.

snapshot.quote: You can back up your Mac mini using a backup solution of your choice. Examples include: Restic for command-line backups. Arq Backup for graphical interface backups. Both solutions allow you to store backups on our Object Storage.
snapshot.note: No provider-side snapshot/image endpoint for Apple silicon (Go SDK applesilicon v1alpha1 has only create/update/delete/reboot/reinstall/private-network/runner); backup is DIY guest-side software to Object Storage.

pause_resume.quote: Yes, you pay for your Mac mini as long as it is assigned to your account. You must explicitly delete it in the console or via the CLI to stop charges.
pause_resume.note: No stop/pause state exists: billing continues regardless of power state, only full deletion stops charges. Apple silicon API exposes no pause/suspend action.

fork.note: API manages only the bare-metal Mac lifecycle (create/update/delete/reboot/reinstall/private-network/runner). No fork/clone-from-running or image-based instantiation endpoint exists; each server is a dedicated physical Mac.

fork_running.note: Same API surface as fork: no live-fork-from-running-instance capability; whole physical Mac minis cannot be forked.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-snapshot or VM-fork feature for bare-metal Apple silicon; the product has no snapshot/image endpoint at all.

computer_use.quote: The pre-installed tools on MacOS include: The latest Xcode version compatible with the OS, MacPorts for package management, fail2ban for VNC access filtering, scw-agent...
computer_use.note: Access is plain VNC/SSH to a bare Mac mini; there is no first-party computer-use/agent-control API (screenshot+click action loop) offered on top of it.

custom_image.quote: To reinstall your Mac mini... you will be prompted to choose the macOS version for the reinstallation process... Switching between OS families during reinstallation is not supported. You cannot reinstall macOS over Asahi Linux, or Asahi Linux over macOS.
custom_image.note: Reinstall only lets you pick a stock macOS version or Asahi Linux; there is no upload-your-own-image / custom OS image mechanism.

wake_on_request.quote: Yes, you pay for your Mac mini as long as it is assigned to your account. You must explicitly delete it in the console or via the CLI to stop charges.
wake_on_request.note: No serverless/wake-on-request model; the Mac stays allocated (and billed) whether powered on or off until explicitly deleted.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Yes, you pay for your Mac mini as long as it is assigned to your account. You must explicitly delete it in the console or via the CLI to stop charges.
auto_stop_idle.note: No idle auto-stop/auto-delete feature; billing runs continuously until manual deletion regardless of activity.

volumes.quote: Block Storage volumes are compatible with Scaleway Instances, Managed Dabatase for PostgreSQL and MySQL, and Kubernetes Kapsule clusters.
volumes.note: Block Storage explicitly lists compatible products and Apple silicon is not one of them; storage is the Mac mini's fixed internal SSD only.

inbound_https.quote: For some products, e.g. Apple silicon, public connectivity cannot be disabled at any stage
inbound_https.note: The Mac mini gets a raw public IPv4/IPv6 with no managed ingress/load-balancer/HTTPS-termination layer; any HTTPS endpoint would have to be self-run on the guest OS, so there is no first-party inbound_https feature.

agent_harnesses.note: API manages the bare-metal Mac lifecycle only (servers, OS, commitment, bandwidth, Private Networks, CI runners via Dev OS); no agent-harness or exec/action API.

gpu.quote: M1-M: M1 8-core, 8 GB, 256 GB (EUR 0.11/h) ... M4-XL: M4 Pro 14-core, 64 GB, 2.05 TB (EUR 0.49/h)
gpu.note: Product is a fixed lineup of Mac mini shapes (Apple M1/M2/M4 SoC only); no discrete/add-on GPU option is sold or documented for this product, unlike Scaleway's separate NVIDIA GPU Instances line.

windows.quote: you will be prompted to choose the macOS version for the reinstallation process... You cannot reinstall macOS over Asahi Linux, or Asahi Linux over macOS.
windows.note: Reinstall OS choices are limited to macOS versions or Asahi Linux; Windows is not an offered OS for Apple silicon Mac minis (Apple hardware/licensing does not support Windows on Apple Silicon here).

self_host.note: This is a hosted rental of Scaleway-owned physical Mac minis in Scaleway's own datacenter (Paris); there is no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option for this product.

byoc.note: Bare-metal Mac minis are rented only in Scaleway's own facilities (Paris AZs); there is no bring-your-own-cloud/deploy-in-your-account model.

open_source.note: Apple silicon is a proprietary managed cloud offering (closed API/console for a commercial rental service); no open-source release of the platform itself.

usage_api.quote: Run the following command to obtain your consumption for a specific project only. First, choose your target project_id: export SCW_PROJECT_ID=... Then: curl -X GET -H X-Auth-Token -H Content-Type https://api.scaleway.com/billing/v2beta1/consumptions?project_id=SCW_PROJECT_ID
usage_api.note: granularity: per-project; cost: yes; Scaleway Billing API v2beta1 provides consumption data via REST with organization_id, project_id, category_name, and billing_period filters. Apple silicon servers can be isolated via project assignment for per-machine billing. API returns cost in Money type (currency + amount).

locations_quote: Mac mini M1 are available in PARIS 3; M2/M2 Pro/M4 in fr-par-1 only. All run in Scaleway's eu (Paris) region.
